body.x: Intel introduced Realsense, the new technology of device control, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.
(Video: Visitors trying out Realsense bu making virtual sand man and playing video game by motions and gestures at Realsense demo hall)

RealSense technology of software and depth cameras enables more natural and intuitive interaction with personal computing devices. Cutting-edge facial detection and tracking, emotion detection, 3D scanning, depth-sensing photography, background removal, and the tracking of 22 joints in each hand for accurate touch-free gesture recognition are some of the new capabilities made possible with Intel RealSense technology.
Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics
exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
